# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# solana_sdk - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/

## Expand description

The Solana host and client SDK.

This is the base library for all off-chain programs that interact with
Solana or otherwise operate on Solana data structures. On-chain programs
instead use the [ solana-program](https://docs.rs/solana-program) crate, the modules of which are
re-exported by this crate, like the relationship between the Rust

`core` and `std` crates. As much of the functionality of this crate is
provided by `solana-program`, see that crate’s documentation for an
overview.Many of the modules in this crate are primarily of use to the Solana runtime
itself. Additional crates provide capabilities built on `solana-sdk`, and
many programs will need to link to those crates as well, particularly for
clients communicating with Solana nodes over RPC.

Such crates include:

- `solana-client`- [JSON-RPC API](https://solana.com/docs/rpc).
- `solana-cli-config`
- `solana-clap-utils`- `clap`

# Address in solana_address - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-address/1.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_address/struct.Address.html

`pub struct Address(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The address of a [Solana account](https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts).

Some account addresses are [ed25519](https://ed25519.cr.yp.to/) public keys, with corresponding secret
keys that are managed off-chain. Often, though, account addresses do not
have corresponding secret keys — as with [ program derived
addresses](https://solana.com/docs/core/cpi#program-derived-addresses) — or the secret key is not relevant to the operation
of a program, and may have even been disposed of. As running Solana programs
can not safely create or manage secret keys, the full

[is not defined in](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/signer/keypair/struct.Keypair.html)

`Keypair``solana-program` but in `solana-sdk`.## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Find a valid [program derived address](https://solana.com/docs/core/cpi#program-derived-addresses) and its corresponding bump seed.

Program derived addresses (PDAs) are account keys that only the program,
`program_id`, has the authority to sign. The address is of the same form
as a Solana `Address`, except they are ensured to not be on the ed25519
curve and thus have no associated private key. When performing
cross-program invocations the program can “sign” for the key by calling
[ invoke_signed](https://docs.rs/solana-program/latest/solana_program/program/fn.invoke_signed.html) and passing the same seeds used to generate the
address, along with the calculated

*bump seed*, which this function returns as the second tuple element. The runtime will verify that the program associated with this address is the caller and thus authorized to be the signer.

The `seeds` are application-specific, and must be carefully selected to
uniquely derive accounts per application requirements. It is common to
use static strings and other addresses as seeds.

Because the program address must not lie on the ed25519 curve, there may
be seed and program id combinations that are invalid. For this reason,
an extra seed (the bump seed) is calculated that results in a
point off the curve. The bump seed must be passed as an additional seed
when calling `invoke_signed`.

The processes of finding a valid program address is by trial and error, and even though it is deterministic given a set of inputs it can take a variable amount of time to succeed across different inputs. This means that when called from an on-chain program it may incur a variable amount of the program’s compute budget. Programs that are meant to be very performant may not want to use this function because it could take a considerable amount of time. Programs that are already at risk of exceeding their compute budget should call this with care since there is a chance that the program’s budget may be occasionally and unpredictably exceeded.

As all account addresses accessed by an on-chain Solana program must be
explicitly passed to the program, it is typical for the PDAs to be
derived in off-chain client programs, avoiding the compute cost of
generating the address on-chain. The address may or may not then be
verified by re-deriving it on-chain, depending on the requirements of
the program. This verification may be performed without the overhead of
re-searching for the bump key by using the [ create_program_address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.create_program_address)
function.

**Warning**: Because of the way the seeds are hashed there is a potential
for program address collisions for the same program id.  The seeds are
hashed sequentially which means that seeds {“abcdef”}, {“abc”, “def”},
and {“ab”, “cd”, “ef”} will all result in the same program address given
the same program id. Since the chance of collision is local to a given
program id, the developer of that program must take care to choose seeds
that do not collide with each other. For seed schemes that are susceptible
to this type of hash collision, a common remedy is to insert separators
between seeds, e.g. transforming {“abc”, “def”} into {“abc”, “-”, “def”}.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics in the statistically improbable event that a bump seed could not be
found. Use [ try_find_program_address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.try_find_program_address) to handle this case.

Panics if any of the following are true:

- the number of provided seeds is greater than, *or equal to*,`crate::MAX_SEEDS`
- any individual seed’s length is greater than `crate::MAX_SEED_LEN`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

This example illustrates a simple case of creating a “vault” account which is derived from the payer account, but owned by an on-chain program. The program derived address is derived in an off-chain client program, which invokes an on-chain Solana program that uses the address to create a new account owned and controlled by the program itself.

By convention, the on-chain program will be compiled for use in two different contexts: both on-chain, to interpret a custom program instruction as a Solana transaction; and off-chain, as a library, so that clients can share the instruction data structure, constructors, and other common code.

First the on-chain Solana program:

```
// The custom instruction processed by our program. It includes the
// PDA's bump seed, which is derived by the client program. This
// definition is also imported into the off-chain client program.
// The computed address of the PDA will be passed to this program via
// the `accounts` vector of the `Instruction` type.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize, Debug)]
pub struct InstructionData {
    pub vault_bump_seed: u8,
    pub lamports: u64,
}
// The size in bytes of a vault account. The client program needs
// this information to calculate the quantity of lamports necessary
// to pay for the account's rent.
pub static VAULT_ACCOUNT_SIZE: u64 = 1024;
// The entrypoint of the on-chain program, as provided to the
// `entrypoint!` macro.
fn process_instruction(
    program_id: &Address,
    accounts: &[AccountInfo],
    instruction_data: &[u8],
) -> ProgramResult {
    let account_info_iter = &mut accounts.iter();
    let payer = next_account_info(account_info_iter)?;
    // The vault PDA, derived from the payer's address
    let vault = next_account_info(account_info_iter)?;
    let mut instruction_data = instruction_data;
    let instr = InstructionData::deserialize(&mut instruction_data)?;
    let vault_bump_seed = instr.vault_bump_seed;
    let lamports = instr.lamports;
    let vault_size = VAULT_ACCOUNT_SIZE;
    // Invoke the system program to create an account while virtually
    // signing with the vault PDA, which is owned by this caller program.
    invoke_signed(
        &create_account(
            &payer.key,
            &vault.key,
            lamports,
            vault_size,
            program_id,
        ),
        &[
            payer.clone(),
            vault.clone(),
        ],
        // A slice of seed slices, each seed slice being the set
        // of seeds used to generate one of the PDAs required by the
        // callee program, the final seed being a single-element slice
        // containing the `u8` bump seed.
        &[
            &[
                b"vault",
                payer.key.as_ref(),
                &[vault_bump_seed],
            ],
        ]
    )?;
    Ok(())
}
```
The client program:

```
fn create_vault_account(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Address,
    payer: &Keypair,
) -> Result<()> {
    // Derive the PDA from the payer account, a string representing the unique
    // purpose of the account ("vault"), and the address of our on-chain program.
    let (vault_address, vault_bump_seed) = Address::find_program_address(
        &[b"vault", payer.pubkey().as_ref()],
        &program_id
    );
    // Get the amount of lamports needed to pay for the vault's rent
    let vault_account_size = usize::try_from(VAULT_ACCOUNT_SIZE)?;
    let lamports = client.get_minimum_balance_for_rent_exemption(vault_account_size)?;
    // The on-chain program's instruction data, imported from that program's crate.
    let instr_data = InstructionData {
        vault_bump_seed,
        lamports,
    };
    // The accounts required by both our on-chain program and the system program's
    // `create_account` instruction, including the vault's address.
    let accounts = vec![
        AccountMeta::new(payer.pubkey(), true),
        AccountMeta::new(vault_address, false),
        AccountMeta::new(solana_system_interface::program::ID, false),
    ];
    // Create the instruction by serializing our instruction data via borsh
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &instr_data,
        accounts,
    );
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    let transaction = Transaction::new_signed_with_payer(
        &[instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
        &[payer],
        blockhash,
    );
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&transaction)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-address/2.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_address/syscalls.rs.html#299-302)

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-address/2.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_address/syscalls.rs.html#299-302)

Find a valid [program derived address](https://solana.com/docs/core/cpi#program-derived-addresses) and its corresponding bump seed.

The only difference between this method and [ find_program_address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.find_program_address)
is that this one returns

`None` in the statistically improbable event
that a bump seed cannot be found; or if any of `find_program_address`’s
preconditions are violated.See the documentation for [ find_program_address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.find_program_address) for a full description.

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-address/2.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_address/syscalls.rs.html#391-394)#### pub fn [create_program_address](https://docs.rs#method.create_program_address)(
    seeds: &[&[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]],
    program_id: &[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html), [AddressError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.AddressError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-address/2.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_address/syscalls.rs.html#391-394)

#### pub fn [create_program_address](https://docs.rs#method.create_program_address)(
    seeds: &[&[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]],
    program_id: &[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html), [AddressError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.AddressError.html)>

Create a valid [program derived address](https://solana.com/docs/core/cpi#program-derived-addresses) without searching for a bump seed.

Because this function does not create a bump seed, it may unpredictably return an error for any given set of seeds and is not generally suitable for creating program derived addresses.

However, it can be used for efficiently verifying that a set of seeds plus
bump seed generated by [ find_program_address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.find_program_address) derives a particular
address as expected. See the example for details.

See the documentation for [ find_program_address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.find_program_address) for a full description
of program derived addresses and bump seeds.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

Creating a program derived address involves iteratively searching for a
bump seed for which the derived [ Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html) does not lie on the ed25519
curve. This search process is generally performed off-chain, with the

[function, after which the client passes the bump seed to the program as instruction data.](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html#method.find_program_address)

`find_program_address`Depending on the application requirements, a program may wish to verify that the set of seeds, plus the bump seed, do correctly generate an expected address.

The verification is performed by appending to the other seeds one
additional seed slice that contains the single `u8` bump seed, calling
`create_program_address`, checking that the return value is `Ok`, and
that the returned `Address` has the expected value.

```
let (expected_pda, bump_seed) = Address::find_program_address(&[b"vault"], &program_id);
let actual_pda = Address::create_program_address(&[b"vault", &[bump_seed]], &program_id)?;
assert_eq!(expected_pda, actual_pda);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-keypair/3.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_keypair/lib.rs.html#77)#### pub fn [insecure_clone](https://docs.rs#method.insecure_clone)(&self) -> [Keypair](https://docs.rs/struct.Keypair.html)

#### pub fn [insecure_clone](https://docs.rs#method.insecure_clone)(&self) -> [Keypair](https://docs.rs/struct.Keypair.html)

Allows Keypair cloning

Note that the `Clone` trait is intentionally unimplemented because making a
second copy of sensitive secret keys in memory is usually a bad idea.

Only use this in tests or when strictly required. Consider using [ std::sync::Arc<Keypair>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)
instead.

# bincode 3.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/bincode

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/bincode/latest/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

# Bincode is now unmaintained

Due to a doxxing and harassment incident, development on bincode has ceased. No further releases will be published on crates.io.

As crates.io, unlike many other language-attached package management solutions, lacks the ability to mark a project as archive or remove the last maintainer, this final release is being published containing only this README, as well as a lib.rs containing only a compiler error, to inform potential users of the maintenance status of this crate.

If you were considering using bincode for a new project or are looking to an alternative to migrate to, you are encouraged to consider some the following alternatives, as well as the many other great serialization format crates available in the rust ecosystem:

-
Bincode-compatible alternative
-
Similar in spirit and structure to bincode, but a bit differently flavored
-
Zero copy deserialization, honestly the best option for many of the usecases that bincode was intended for, like serializing transient data for intra-program message passing.

# What the community can do better

Several tooling factors have lead to bincode's maintenance status being a bigger issue than it needs to be, including:

-
crates.io not having functionality for marking a package unmaintained or a process for the crates.io maintainers to transfer ownership of an abandoned package to a prospective maintainer In many other programming language communities such as haskell and hackage, or python and pypi, when the last maintainer of a critical crate just walks away, there often an in-band status that identifies that package as having no active maintainers, and usually at least *some*policy in place for the package collection maintainers to intervene and transfer ownership of such a package, allowing the community to assign a new maintainer to the existing package, automatically pointing the rest of the ecosystem to the new sources with no intervention required on the consumers part.crates.io not having any such functionality or processes creates a pretty massive pain point when the last maintainer does walk away, placing the burden on *them*, very often an already burnt out volunteer, to select a new maintainer. If the existing maintainer does not do this, the only current way to continue maintenance of the package is to create a differently-named fork, and then go through the massive hassle of not only convincing the entire ecosystem to use it, but to settle in on one community preferred fork. This creates avoidable tension when maintainers*do*just walk away, with community members being scared to make the fork themselves, both out of fear of the amount of work getting the community to adopt it entails, and out of fear of making the inevitable fork-fight worse by adding another contestant.
-
crates.io not having visibility for its internal source control Much of the drama that resulted in the doxxing and harassment was centered around the git history being rewritten when the repository was blanked out on github and moved to sourcehut. While this is a legitimate cause for some level of concern that merits at least asking a question, it is disappointing that the community is focusing on it so much when virtually none of the users of bincode are pulling from the git version anyway, with almost all of the users using the crates.io release. While the existing bincode releases are tied to the previous history through the git commit reference cargo release's `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, the cargo releases, which represent the canonical version of bincode, are not fundamentally tied to the git repository at all, and there has been a lot of worrying about*the wrong supply chain*.We have faced many questions like "if the github is deleted, where can users make sure they are getting the old version of the source code" that are answered with "there haven't been any crates.io releases since the migration and history rewrite, just bring in an old version with cargo and you'll have it". This could have been potentially avoided if crates.io and cargo provided better visibility into their internal source control used for packing crates. At the very least, a link to the source code browser on docs.rs from the crates.io page for a given release could have made more users aware of the fact that crates.io/cargo provide such internal source control, and a full on source code viewer, or even better a version comparison tool, integrated into crates.io would have made things a *lot*more manageable while there were still such questions flying around.
-
crates.io metadata is not editable without performing a release Much of this could have been avoided if the crates.io metadata was independently editable and included a contact information field (ideally something like githubs private email solution, where it provides a generated email address that forwards to something configurable). At the time of migration, bincode was nowhere *near*ready for another release, and being able to independently update the source code link in the crates.io metadata and provide up to date contact information without having to roll either a special no-code-changes release off of a branch that only changed those things, or roll a questionable intermediate release with the changes, both of which likely would have only raised more concerns from the community, would have significantly decreased the developer burden of completing the migration in a public and notorious fashion.

---

# Transaction in solana_sdk::transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/transaction/struct.Transaction.html

**crate feature**only.

`full`## Expand description

An atomically-committed sequence of instructions.

While [ Instruction](https://docs.rs/instruction/struct.Instruction.html)s are the basic unit of computation in Solana,
they are submitted by clients in

[s containing one or more instructions, and signed by one or more](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html)

`Transaction`[s.](https://docs.rs/solana-signer/latest/solana_signer/trait.Signer.html)

`Signer`See the [module documentation](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_transaction/index.html) for more details about transactions.

Some constructors accept an optional `payer`, the account responsible for
paying the cost of executing a transaction. In most cases, callers should
specify the payer explicitly in these constructors. In some cases though,
the caller is not *required* to specify the payer, but is still allowed to:
in the [ Message](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html) structure, the first account is always the fee-payer, so
if the caller has knowledge that the first account of the constructed
transaction’s

`Message` is both a signer and the expected fee-payer, then
redundantly specifying the fee-payer is not strictly required.## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.signatures)

`signatures: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Signature](https://docs.rs/signature/struct.Signature.html)>A set of signatures of a serialized [ Message](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html), signed by the first
keys of the

`Message`’s [, where the number of signatures is equal to](https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.account_keys)

`account_keys`[of the](https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/struct.MessageHeader.html#structfield.num_required_signatures)

`num_required_signatures``Message`’s
[.](https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/struct.MessageHeader.html)

`MessageHeader`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.message)

`message: `[Message](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html)The message to sign.

#### pub fn [new_unsigned](https://docs.rs#method.new_unsigned)(message: [Message](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html)) -> [Transaction](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html)

Create an unsigned transaction from a [ Message](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_rpc_client](https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client) and

[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Pubkey,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let message = Message::new(
        &[instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
    );
    let mut tx = Transaction::new_unsigned(message);
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    tx.sign(&[payer], blockhash);
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `from_keypairs`- The keys used to sign the transaction.
- `keys`- The keys for the transaction. These are the program state instances or lamport recipient keys.
- `recent_blockhash`- The PoH hash.
- `program_ids`- The keys that identify programs used in the- `instruction`vector.
- `instructions`- Instructions that will be executed atomically.

description of failure conditions.

The `instruction_index` corresponds to the [ instructions](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.instructions) vector of
the

`Transaction`’s [value.](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

instructions in the transaction.

the transaction.

the

`Transaction`’s [value; and the](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#620)#### pub fn [signer_key](https://docs.rs#method.signer_key)(

    accounts_index: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Address](https://docs.rs/entrypoint/struct.__Pubkey.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#620)

#### pub fn [signer_key](https://docs.rs#method.signer_key)(
    &self,
    instruction_index: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    accounts_index: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Address](https://docs.rs/entrypoint/struct.__Pubkey.html)>

Get the `Pubkey` of a signing account required by one of the
instructions in the transaction.

The transaction does not need to be signed for this function to return a signing account’s pubkey.

Returns `None` if the indexed account is not required to sign the
transaction. Returns `None` if the [ signatures](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#structfield.signatures) field does not contain
enough elements to hold a signature for the indexed account (this should
only be possible if

`Transaction` has been manually constructed).Returns `None` if `instruction_index` is greater than or equal to the
number of instructions in the transaction; or if `accounts_index` is
greater than or equal to the number of accounts in the instruction.

Return the message containing all data that should be signed.

**crate feature **`wincode` only.

`wincode`Return the serialized message data to sign.

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#720)**crate feature **`wincode` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#720)

**crate feature**only.

`wincode`Sign the transaction.

This method fully signs a transaction with all required signers, which
must be present in the `keypairs` slice. To sign with only some of the
required signers, use [ Transaction::partial_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.partial_sign).

If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message’s
[ recent_blockhash](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.recent_blockhash) field, then the message’s

`recent_blockhash` will be updated
to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics when signing fails. Use [ Transaction::try_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_sign) to handle the
error. See the documentation for

[for a full description of failure conditions.](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_sign)

`Transaction::try_sign`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_rpc_client](https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client) and

[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Pubkey,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let mut tx = Transaction::new_with_payer(&[instruction], Some(&payer.pubkey()));
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    tx.sign(&[payer], blockhash);
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

#### pub fn [partial_sign](https://docs.rs#method.partial_sign)<T>(&mut self, keypairs: [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), recent_blockhash: [Hash](https://docs.rs/hash/struct.Hash.html))

`wincode`Sign the transaction with a subset of required keys.

Unlike [ Transaction::sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.sign), this method does not require all keypairs
to be provided, allowing a transaction to be signed in multiple steps.

It is permitted to sign a transaction with the same keypair multiple times.

If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message’s
[ recent_blockhash](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.recent_blockhash) field, then the message’s

`recent_blockhash` will be updated
to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-5)Panics

Panics when signing fails. Use [ Transaction::try_partial_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign) to
handle the error. See the documentation for

[for a full description of failure conditions.](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign)

`Transaction::try_partial_sign`[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#767-772)#### pub fn [partial_sign_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.partial_sign_unchecked)<T>(

    keypairs: [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#767-772)

#### pub fn [partial_sign_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.partial_sign_unchecked)<T>(
    &mut self,
    keypairs: [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
    positions: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
    recent_blockhash: [Hash](https://docs.rs/hash/struct.Hash.html),
)

**crate feature**only.

`wincode`Sign the transaction with a subset of required keys.

This places each of the signatures created from `keypairs` in the
corresponding position, as specified in the `positions` vector, in the
transactions [ signatures](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#structfield.signatures) field. It does not verify that the signature
positions are correct.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-6)Panics

Panics if signing fails. Use [ Transaction::try_partial_sign_unchecked](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign_unchecked)
to handle the error.

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#860-864)**crate feature **`wincode` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#860-864)

**crate feature**only.

`wincode`Sign the transaction, returning any errors.

This method fully signs a transaction with all required signers, which
must be present in the `keypairs` slice. To sign with only some of the
required signers, use [ Transaction::try_partial_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign).

If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message’s
[ recent_blockhash](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.recent_blockhash) field, then the message’s

`recent_blockhash` will be updated
to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Signing will fail if some required signers are not provided in
`keypairs`; or, if the transaction has previously been partially signed,
some of the remaining required signers are not provided in `keypairs`.
In other words, the transaction must be fully signed as a result of
calling this function. The error is [ SignerError::NotEnoughSigners](https://docs.rs/signer/enum.SignerError.html#variant.NotEnoughSigners).

Signing will fail for any of the reasons described in the documentation
for [ Transaction::try_partial_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_rpc_client](https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client) and

[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Pubkey,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let mut tx = Transaction::new_with_payer(&[instruction], Some(&payer.pubkey()));
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    tx.try_sign(&[payer], blockhash)?;
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`wincode`Sign the transaction with a subset of required keys, returning any errors.

Unlike [ Transaction::try_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_sign), this method does not require all
keypairs to be provided, allowing a transaction to be signed in multiple
steps.

It is permitted to sign a transaction with the same keypair multiple times.

If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message’s
[ recent_blockhash](https://docs.rs/solana-message/4.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.recent_blockhash) field, then the message’s

`recent_blockhash` will be updated
to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

Signing will fail if

- The transaction’s `Message``num_required_signatures``account_keys``SignerError::TransactionError``TransactionError``TransactionError::InvalidAccountIndex`
- Any of the provided signers in `keypairs`is not a required signer of the message. The error is`SignerError::KeypairPubkeyMismatch`
- Any of the signers is a `Presigner``SignerError::PresignerError``PresignerError``PresignerError::VerificationFailure`
- The signer is a `RemoteKeypair`- It does not understand the input provided (`SignerError::InvalidInput`
- The device cannot be found (`SignerError::NoDeviceFound`
- The user cancels the signing (`SignerError::UserCancel`
- An error was encountered connecting (`SignerError::Connection`
- Some device-specific protocol error occurs (`SignerError::Protocol`
- Some other error occurs (`SignerError::Custom`

- It does not understand the input provided (

See the documentation for the [ solana-remote-wallet](https://docs.rs/solana-remote-wallet/latest/) crate for details
on the operation of

[signers.](https://docs.rs/solana-remote-wallet/latest/solana_remote_wallet/remote_keypair/struct.RemoteKeypair.html)

# solana_system_interface::instruction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-system-interface/latest/solana_system_interface/instruction/index.html

## Expand description

Instructions and constructors for the system program.

The system program is responsible for the creation of accounts and [nonce
accounts](https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/durable-tx-nonces). It is responsible for transferring lamports from accounts
owned by the system program, including typical user wallet accounts.

Account creation typically involves three steps: [ allocate](https://docs.rs/fn.allocate.html) space,

[lamports for rent,](https://docs.rs/fn.transfer.html)

`transfer`[to its owning program. The](https://docs.rs/fn.assign.html)

`assign`[function does all three at once. All new accounts must contain enough lamports to be](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account.html)

`create_account`[rent exempt](https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts#rent-exemption), or else the creation instruction will fail.

The [ create_account](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account.html) function requires that the account have zero
lamports.

[allows for the account to have lamports prefunded; note that without feature activation of](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account_allow_prefund.html)

`create_account_allow_prefund`[SIMD-0312](https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-improvement-documents/pull/312),

[will fail downstream.](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account_allow_prefund.html)

`create_account_allow_prefund`The accounts created by the System program can either be user-controlled,
where the secret keys are held outside the blockchain,
or they can be [program derived addresses](https://docs.rs/solana-address/latest/solana_address/struct.Address.html#method.find_program_address),
where write access to accounts is granted by an owning program.

Most of the functions in this module construct an [ Instruction](https://docs.rs/solana-instruction/latest/solana_instruction/struct.Instruction.html), that must
be submitted to the runtime for execution, either via RPC, typically with

[, or through](https://docs.rs/solana-client/latest/solana_client/rpc_client/struct.RpcClient.html)

`RpcClient`[cross-program invocation](https://docs.rs/solana-cpi/latest/solana_cpi/index.html).

When invoking through CPI, the [ invoke](https://docs.rs/solana-cpi/latest/solana_cpi/fn.invoke.html) or

[instruction requires all account references to be provided explicitly as](https://docs.rs/solana-cpi/latest/solana_cpi/fn.invoke_signed.html)

`invoke_signed`[values. The account references required are specified in the documentation for the](https://docs.rs/solana-account-info/latest/solana_account_info/struct.AccountInfo.html)

`AccountInfo`[variants for each System program instruction, and these variants are linked from the documentation for their constructors.](https://docs.rs/enum.SystemInstruction.html)

`SystemInstruction`## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [System](https://docs.rs/enum.SystemInstruction.html)- Instruction
- An instruction to the system program.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [advance_](https://docs.rs/fn.advance_nonce_account.html)- nonce_ - account - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Advance the value of a durable transaction nonce.
- [allocate](https://docs.rs/fn.allocate.html)- `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Allocate space for an account.
- [allocate_](https://docs.rs/fn.allocate_with_seed.html)- with_ - seed - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- [assign](https://docs.rs/fn.assign.html)- `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Assign ownership of an account from the system program.
- [assign_](https://docs.rs/fn.assign_with_seed.html)- with_ - seed - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- [authorize_](https://docs.rs/fn.authorize_nonce_account.html)- nonce_ - account - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Change the authority of a durable transaction nonce account.
- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account.html)- account - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Create an account, failing if the account previously had any balance.
- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account_allow_prefund.html)- account_ - allow_ - prefund - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Create a new account without enforcing zero lamports on the destination account.
- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_account_with_seed.html)- account_ - with_ - seed - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_nonce_account.html)- nonce_ - account - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Create an account containing a durable transaction nonce.
- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_nonce_account_with_seed.html)- nonce_ - account_ - with_ - seed - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- [transfer](https://docs.rs/fn.transfer.html)- `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Transfer lamports from an account owned by the system program.
- [transfer_](https://docs.rs/fn.transfer_many.html)- many - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Transfer lamports from an account owned by the system program to multiple accounts.
- [transfer_](https://docs.rs/fn.transfer_with_seed.html)- with_ - seed - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- [upgrade_](https://docs.rs/fn.upgrade_nonce_account.html)- nonce_ - account - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- One-time idempotent upgrade of legacy nonce versions in order to bump them out of chain blockhash domain.
- [withdraw_](https://docs.rs/fn.withdraw_nonce_account.html)- nonce_ - account - `bincode`or- `wincode`
- Withdraw lamports from a durable transaction nonce account.

Compute Budget Instructions

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unused)

### Unused

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RequestHeapFrame)

### RequestHeapFrame([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

Request a specific transaction-wide program heap region size in bytes. The value requested must be a multiple of 1024. This new heap region size applies to each program executed in the transaction, including all calls to CPIs.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SetComputeUnitLimit)

### SetComputeUnitLimit([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

Set a specific compute unit limit that the transaction is allowed to consume.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SetComputeUnitPrice)

### SetComputeUnitPrice([u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

Set a compute unit price in “micro-lamports” to pay a higher transaction fee for higher transaction prioritization.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SetLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit)

### SetLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

Set a specific transaction-wide account data size limit, in bytes, is allowed to load.

# solana_program_pack - Rust

## Expand description

The [ Pack](https://docs.rs/trait.Pack.html) serialization trait
This is a specific serialization API that is used by many older programs in
the

[Solana Program Library](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana-program-library)to manage account state. It is not generally recommended for new code since it does not define a language-independent serialization format.

- [IsInitialized](https://docs.rs/trait.IsInitialized.html)
- Check if a program account state is initialized
- [Pack](https://docs.rs/trait.Pack.html)
- Safely and efficiently (de)serialize account state
- [Sealed](https://docs.rs/trait.Sealed.html)
- Implementors must have a known size

## Expand description

Compact serde-encoding of vectors with small length.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Short](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortU16.html)- U16
- Same as u16, but serialized with 1 to 3 bytes. If the value is above 0x7f, the top bit is set and the remaining value is stored in the next bytes. Each byte follows the same pattern until the 3rd byte. The 3rd byte may only have the 2 least-significant bits set, otherwise the encoded value will overflow the u16.
- [Short](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortVec.html)- Vec

- If you don’t want to use the ShortVec newtype, you can do ShortVec deserialization on an ordinary vector with the following field annotation:

# solana_clock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-clock/3.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/solana_clock/index.html

## Expand description

Information about the network’s clock, ticks, slots, etc.

Time in Solana is marked primarily by *slots*, which occur approximately every
400 milliseconds, and are numbered sequentially. For every slot, a leader is
chosen from the validator set, and that leader is expected to produce a new
block, though sometimes leaders may fail to do so. Blocks can be identified
by their slot number, and some slots do not contain a block.

An approximation of the passage of real-world time can be calculated by
multiplying a number of slots by [ DEFAULT_MS_PER_SLOT](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_MS_PER_SLOT.html), which is a constant target
time for the network to produce slots. Note though that this method suffers
a variable amount of drift, as the network does not produce slots at exactly
the target rate, and the greater number of slots being calculated for, the
greater the drift. Epochs cannot be used this way as they contain variable
numbers of slots.

The network’s current view of the real-world time can always be accessed via
[ Clock::unix_timestamp](https://docs.rs/struct.Clock.html#structfield.unix_timestamp), which is produced by an

[oracle derived from the validator set](https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/validator-timestamp-oracle).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [sysvar](https://docs.rs/sysvar/index.html)- `sysvar`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Clock](https://docs.rs/struct.Clock.html)
- A representation of network time.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_DEV_SLOTS_PER_EPOCH.html)- DEV_ - SLOTS_ - PER_ - EPOCH
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_HASHES_PER_SECOND.html)- HASHES_ - PER_ - SECOND
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_HASHES_PER_TICK.html)- HASHES_ - PER_ - TICK
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_MS_PER_SLOT.html)- MS_ - PER_ - SLOT
- The expected duration of a slot (400 milliseconds).
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_SLOTS_PER_EPOCH.html)- SLOTS_ - PER_ - EPOCH
- The number of slots per epoch after initial network warmup.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_S_PER_SLOT.html)- S_ - PER_ - SLOT
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_TICKS_PER_SECOND.html)- TICKS_ - PER_ - SECOND
- The default tick rate that the cluster attempts to achieve (160 per second).
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_TICKS_PER_SLOT.html)- TICKS_ - PER_ - SLOT
- [FORWARD_](https://docs.rs/constant.FORWARD_TRANSACTIONS_TO_LEADER_AT_SLOT_OFFSET.html)- TRANSACTIONS_ - TO_ - LEADER_ - AT_ - SLOT_ - OFFSET
- Transaction forwarding, which leader to forward to and how long to hold
- [GENESIS_](https://docs.rs/constant.GENESIS_EPOCH.html)- EPOCH
- [HOLD_](https://docs.rs/constant.HOLD_TRANSACTIONS_SLOT_OFFSET.html)- TRANSACTIONS_ - SLOT_ - OFFSET
- [INITIAL_](https://docs.rs/constant.INITIAL_RENT_EPOCH.html)- RENT_ - EPOCH
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_HASH_AGE_IN_SECONDS.html)- HASH_ - AGE_ - IN_ - SECONDS
- The time window of recent block hash values over which the bank will track signatures.
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_PROCESSING_AGE.html)- PROCESSING_ - AGE
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_RECENT_BLOCKHASHES.html)- RECENT_ - BLOCKHASHES
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_TRANSACTION_FORWARDING_DELAY.html)- TRANSACTION_ - FORWARDING_ - DELAY
- More delay is expected if CUDA is not enabled (as signature verification takes longer)
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_TRANSACTION_FORWARDING_DELAY_GPU.html)- TRANSACTION_ - FORWARDING_ - DELAY_ - GPU
- This is maximum time consumed in forwarding a transaction from one node to next, before it can be processed in the target node
- [MS_](https://docs.rs/constant.MS_PER_TICK.html)- PER_ - TICK
- The number of milliseconds per tick (6).
- [NUM_](https://docs.rs/constant.NUM_CONSECUTIVE_LEADER_SLOTS.html)- CONSECUTIVE_ - LEADER_ - SLOTS
- [SECONDS_](https://docs.rs/constant.SECONDS_PER_DAY.html)- PER_ - DAY
- [TICKS_](https://docs.rs/constant.TICKS_PER_DAY.html)- PER_ - DAY

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [BankId](https://docs.rs/type.BankId.html)
- Uniquely distinguishes every version of a slot.
- [Epoch](https://docs.rs/type.Epoch.html)
- The unit of time a given leader schedule is honored.
- [Slot](https://docs.rs/type.Slot.html)

# rsclaw-jobs 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rsclaw-jobs/0.1.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/rsclaw-jobs/0.1.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

`rsclaw-jobs` — pure provider-API job layer for async video / image
generation (crate-split, step-12 P2).

Lifted out of `gateway/external_jobs_worker.rs`: the per-provider HTTP
adapters (`submit_*` for the tool side, `poll_*` + `download_artifact`
for the worker side). This crate has NO gateway dependency — it knows
nothing about the task queue, `ExternalJob` persistence, channels, or
shutdown. The gateway-coupled `ExternalJobsWorker` tick/delivery loop
stays in root and calls back into these functions.

This breaks the old agent->gateway edge: `agent::tools_video` now calls
`rsclaw_jobs::submit_*` instead of reaching into the gateway worker.

Adding a new async provider means: add the corresponding `submit_*` for
the tool side and `poll_*` for the worker side, then extend the
`dispatch_poll` match in the gateway worker.

# hanzo-kernel 0.2.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hanzo-kernel/0.2.6

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/hanzo-kernel/0.2.6/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

hanzo-kernel: Hanzo's first-party GPU kernel DSL.

Write a kernel ONCE in Rust; it lowers to CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / Metal. This crate is the
first-party facade over the CubeCL lowering engine: kernel source names only `hanzo_kernel::*`,
never `cubecl`. "Values, not places" -- CubeCL is the implementation value; `hanzo_kernel` is the
stable namespace we build against, so the engine can be upgraded (or forked) without touching a
single kernel.

The perf primitives our hand-tuned kernels rely on are all here and lower to the native instruction on each backend:

- `dot`on a vectorized- `Line<i8>`-> dp4a / OpSDotAccSat (int8 4-way dot)
- `cmma`-> tensor cores (WMMA / cooperative-matrix / simdgroup)
- `SharedMemory`,- `plane_*`(subgroup reduce/shuffle),- `Atomic`, barriers

MIGRATION POLICY (perf-gated, never a downgrade): the DSL provides COVERAGE -- every quant type on every backend, from one source, killing the "same op, N impls, N numeric behaviors" bug class. A hand-tuned kernel is replaced by its DSL twin ONLY when the DSL version is bit-exact AND within perf noise (bench-gated). Where a hand-tuned kernel still wins, it stays as the specialized peak path and the DSL is the portable fallback for the backends that lack a tuned version.

# spanda_sdk - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/spanda-sdk/0.5.5/spanda_sdk/

## Expand description

Official Rust SDK for Spanda — thin HTTP client over Control Center API v1.

Core platform logic lives in Rust runtime crates; this crate delegates to
`spanda-api` REST endpoints without duplicating business rules.

Enable feature `grpc` for a native tonic client.

# sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-scheme/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_scheme/

## Expand description

Scheme (R7RS-small) surface profile for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the codec, eval-policy, and `Expr` contracts; this crate
is a loadable language profile presenting a Scheme surface syntax over the
shared `Expr` graph, not a standalone interpreter.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Located](https://docs.rs/struct.LocatedSchemeLowering.html)- Scheme - Lowering
- A `SchemeLowered`
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeBaseExport.html)- Base - Export
- A Scheme base-library export: a surface symbol and its description.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeCodec.html)- Codec
- Decoder turning Scheme surface text into the shared `Expr`graph.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeCodecLib.html)- Codec - Lib
- Loadable `Lib``SchemeCodec`
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeFormSpec.html)- Form - Spec
- Specification of one R7RS-small surface form: its symbol, doc, match shape, and support status.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeFormStatus.html)- Form - Status
- Whether a Scheme surface form is supported by this profile.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeLowered.html)- Lowered
- Result of lowering a Scheme `Expr`to a runtime value.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_scheme_tree.html)- scheme_ - tree
- Decodes Scheme surface text into a located `Expr`tree under codec budgets.
- [diagnose_](https://docs.rs/fn.diagnose_unsupported_forms.html)- unsupported_ - forms
- Collects diagnostics for any deferred R7RS-small forms reachable in `expr`.
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_r7rs_small_profile.html)- r7rs_ - small_ - profile
- Installs the R7RS-small profile into a `ProfileRegistry`
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_scheme_expr.html)- scheme_ - expr
- Lowers a single Scheme `Expr`to a`SchemeLowered`
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_scheme_tree.html)- scheme_ - tree
- Lowers a located Scheme tree, preserving its origin.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scheme_source.html)- scheme_ - source
- Parses one top-level Scheme form from source text into a located `Expr`tree.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_scheme_base_claims.html)- scheme_ - base_ - claims
- Publishes idempotent base-export card claims for the supported forms.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_scheme_base_claims_for_lib.html)- scheme_ - base_ - claims_ - for_ - lib
- Publishes base-export card claims as part of a loaded lib receipt.
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_base_exports.html)- small_ - base_ - exports
- Returns the supported R7RS-small forms as base-library exports.
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_expr_cases.html)- small_ - expr_ - cases
- R7RS-small expression round-trip cases for the Scheme row.
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_form_specs.html)- small_ - form_ - specs
- Returns the R7RS-small surface form specifications and their support status.
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_matrix_row.html)- small_ - matrix_ - row
- Builds the Scheme R7RS-small matrix row.
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_profile.html)- small_ - profile
- Builds the R7RS-small `LanguageProfile`
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_profile_symbol.html)- small_ - profile_ - symbol
- Stable identity symbol for the R7RS-small language profile.
- [r7rs_](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_stub_cases.html)- small_ - stub_ - cases
- Minimal R7RS-small source cases for the matrix.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_r7rs_small_conformance_case.html)- r7rs_ - small_ - conformance_ - case
- Runs one Scheme source conformance case through the R7RS-small restricted runner.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_r7rs_small_restricted.html)- r7rs_ - small_ - restricted
- Decodes and lowers Scheme `source`under untrusted, restricted capabilities.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_scheme_matrix_row.html)- scheme_ - matrix_ - row
- Runs the Scheme matrix row and publishes one claim-backed evidence record for each source case.
- [scheme_](https://docs.rs/fn.scheme_base_export_kind_symbol.html)- base_ - export_ - kind_ - symbol
- Card-kind symbol tagging published Scheme base-library exports.
- [scheme_](https://docs.rs/fn.scheme_conformance_test_symbol.html)- conformance_ - test_ - symbol
- Symbol naming the profile’s conformance test.
- [scheme_](https://docs.rs/fn.scheme_language_card.html)- language_ - card
- Builds the Scheme profile Card with browseable conformance fields.
- [scheme_](https://docs.rs/fn.scheme_language_card_with_generated_coverage.html)- language_ - card_ - with_ - generated_ - coverage
- Builds the Scheme profile Card and appends generated coverage fields.
- [scheme_](https://docs.rs/fn.scheme_lowering_symbol.html)- lowering_ - symbol
- Symbol naming the Scheme surface-to-`Expr`lowering pass.
- [scheme_](https://docs.rs/fn.scheme_reader_symbol.html)- reader_ - symbol
- Codec symbol naming the Scheme surface reader.

# a3s 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/a3s/0.6.0

# a3s

The umbrella CLI for the [A3S](https://github.com/A3S-Lab) platform.

`a3s <tool> [args...]` runs the matching A3S tool. `a3s box ...` proxies to
`a3s-box ...` and bootstraps the Box runtime automatically if it is missing:

```
a3s code            # → a3s-code   (launches its TUI)
a3s box ps          # → a3s-box ps (auto-installs a3s-box if needed)
a3s <tool> --help   # a tool's own help
a3s list            # list installed a3s-* tools
a3s --version
```
## Install

```
# from source
# or from this repo
# or Homebrew
```
Then run the tools you need. `a3s box ...` installs `a3s-box` on first use.

## Account Models

In `a3s code`, `/model` lists configured `config.acl` models plus signed-in
account tabs. When Claude Code is logged in (`claude /login`), the Claude Code
tab can switch the current session to Claude models using the local Claude Code
OAuth credentials, including Claude Code's macOS Keychain entry.
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` can also provide the account
token for non-standard environments. If Anthropic rejects the raw OAuth Messages
API bridge with a rate-limit or authentication error, a3s falls back to the
installed `claude` CLI in safe streaming mode; Claude Code's own tools stay
disabled while a3s host tools are requested through an adapter protocol and
still execute inside a3s-code. The adapter accepts Claude Code-style
`<function_calls>` output and tool names such as `Read` or `Bash`, normalizes
common argument aliases like `path` to a3s's `file_path`, and feeds tool results
back into the next Claude turn as structured history.

## Testing

```
```
The ignored soak test repeats `a3s box` after a fake first-use install and
verifies later runs reuse the installed `a3s-box`. The ignored
`ctx_compact_real_llm` test drives the configured model (`~/.a3s/config.acl`)
until the context crosses the auto-compact threshold and asserts streaming
usage is reported, compaction shrinks the history, and the next prompt drops —
the machinery behind the TUI's ctx%, fill warnings, and auto-compaction.

## Updating

In the TUI, ** /update** upgrades to the latest release and restarts into your
session — Homebrew installs are refreshed + upgraded; standalone installs swap
the binary directly. Both paths verify the installed binary reports the target
version before treating the update as successful.

If you're on an **older build (≤ 0.5.4)** whose `/update` was broken, it can't
upgrade itself, and `brew upgrade a3s` alone won't see the new version (Homebrew
doesn't re-sync a tap on `upgrade`). Bootstrap onto a current build once with:

```
 &&
```
From 0.5.5 onward, `/update` handles the tap refresh itself, so this manual step
isn't needed again.

## License

MIT

# a3s_code_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/a3s-code-core/4.2.9/a3s_code_core/

## Expand description

A3S Code Core Library

Harness-driven runtime for coding agents.

`Agent` and `AgentSession` are the primary 2.0 API. Lower-level session
runtime state is internal; persistence data flows through `store::SessionData`.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use a3s_code_core::{Agent, AgentEvent};
// From an ACL-compatible config file path (.acl)
let agent = Agent::new("agent.acl").await?;
// Create a workspace-bound session
let session = agent.session("/my-project", None)?;
// Non-streaming
let result = session.send("What files handle auth?", None).await?;
println!("{}", result.text);
// Streaming (AgentEvent is #[non_exhaustive])
let (mut rx, _handle) = session.stream("Refactor auth", None).await?;
while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await {
    match event {
        AgentEvent::TextDelta { text } => print!("{text}"),
        AgentEvent::End { .. } => break,
        _ => {} // required: #[non_exhaustive]
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#disposable-workers)Disposable Workers

```
use a3s_code_core::{Agent, SessionOptions, WorkerAgentSpec};
let agent = Agent::new("agent.acl").await?;
let frontend = WorkerAgentSpec::implementer(
    "frontend-cow",
    "Small verified frontend fixes",
)
.with_model_ref("openai/gpt-4o")
.with_max_steps(24);
let session = agent.session(
    "/my-project",
    Some(SessionOptions::new().with_worker_agent(frontend)),
)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

```
Agent (config-driven facade)
  +-- AgentSession (workspace-bound execution API)
      +-- internal turn runner
      +-- ContextAssembler / ContextProvider
      +-- ToolSelector
      +-- ToolExecutor
      +-- ProgramExecutor (PTC)
      +-- SkillRegistry
      +-- Permission / confirmation
      +-- Trace / artifacts / verification evidence
Advanced infrastructure:
  +-- optional lane queues for explicit external/hybrid dispatch
```

# euv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv/0.8.15/euv/

## Expand description

euv

A declarative, cross-platform UI framework for Rust with virtual DOM, reactive signals, and HTML macros for WebAssembly.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [console_error_panic_hook](https://docs.rs/console_error_panic_hook/0.1.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/console_error_panic_hook/index.html);
- `pub use`- [js_sys](https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/js_sys/index.html);
- `pub use`- [wasm_bindgen](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/wasm_bindgen/index.html);
- `pub use`- [wasm_bindgen_futures](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen-futures/0.4.76/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/wasm_bindgen_futures/index.html);
- `pub use`- [web_sys](https://docs.rs/web-sys/0.3.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/web_sys/index.html);

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [class](https://docs.rs/macro.class.html)
- The `class!`macro for defining CSS classes with style properties.
- [computed](https://docs.rs/macro.computed.html)
- The `computed!`macro for creating reactive computed signals.
- [html](https://docs.rs/macro.html.html)
- The `html!`macro for writing declarative UI in euv.
- [var](https://docs.rs/macro.var.html)
- The `var!`macro for referencing CSS custom properties defined via`vars!`.
- [vars](https://docs.rs/macro.vars.html)
- The `vars!`macro for defining CSS custom properties.
- [watch](https://docs.rs/macro.watch.html)
- The `watch!`macro for creating reactive side effects.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Attr](https://docs.rs/struct.AttrValueAdapter.html)- Value - Adapter
- Adapts an arbitrary attribute value expression into an `AttributeValue`.
- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/struct.AttributeEntry.html)- Entry
- Represents a single attribute on a virtual DOM node.
- [Callback](https://docs.rs/struct.CallbackNamedAdapter.html)- Named - Adapter
- Adapts a callback with a custom name into an `AttributeValue`.
- [Css](https://docs.rs/struct.Css.html)
- Represents a CSS class with a name, its style declarations, and optional pseudo rules.
- [Dynamic](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamicNode.html)- Node
- A closure-based dynamic node that re-renders when its dependency signals change.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventAdapter.html)- Adapter
- Adapts various event value types into an `AttributeValue`for event attributes.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventNamedAdapter.html)- Named - Adapter
- Adapts an event with a specific event name into an `AttributeValue`.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookContext.html)- Context
- Manages hook state across render cycles for a DynamicNode.
- [Interval](https://docs.rs/struct.IntervalHandle.html)- Handle
- A handle to a browser interval timer created by `use_interval`.
- [Media](https://docs.rs/struct.MediaRule.html)- Rule
- Represents a CSS @media rule attached to a class.
- [Native](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeEventHandler.html)- Event - Handler
- A wrapper around an event callback.
- [Pseudo](https://docs.rs/struct.PseudoRule.html)- Rule
- Represents a CSS pseudo-class or pseudo-element rule attached to a class.
- [Signal](https://docs.rs/struct.Signal.html)
- A reactive signal handle.
- [Signal](https://docs.rs/struct.SignalCell.html)- Cell
- A `Sync`wrapper for single-threaded global`Signal`access.
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextNode.html)- Node
- Represents a text node in the virtual DOM.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)- Value
- Represents the value of an HTML attribute.
- [Tag](https://docs.rs/enum.Tag.html)
- Represents the type of an HTML tag or a component.
- [Virtual](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)- Node
- Represents a node in the virtual DOM tree.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [batch](https://docs.rs/fn.batch.html)
- Batches signal updates within a closure, deferring DOM dispatch until the outermost batch completes.
- [mount](https://docs.rs/fn.mount.html)
- Mounts the given virtual DOM tree to a specific element matched by a CSS selector.
- [schedule_](https://docs.rs/fn.schedule_update.html)- update
- Schedules a deferred signal update with precise dirty marking.
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_cleanup.html)- cleanup
- Registers a cleanup callback that will be executed when the current
hook context is cleared (e.g., when a `match`arm switches).
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_interval.html)- interval
- Creates a recurring interval that invokes the given closure at the
specified period, returning an `IntervalHandle`that is automatically cleared when the hook context is cleared (i.e., when the component unmounts or a`match`arm switches).
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_signal.html)- signal
- Creates a new reactive signal with the given initial value.
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_window_event.html)- window_ - event
- Registers a `window.addEventListener`callback using event delegation, automatically removed when the hook context is cleared.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [component](https://docs.rs/attr.component.html)
- The `component`attribute macro for marking component functions.

# synth-verify - Formal Verification for Synth Compiler

Formal verification infrastructure for the Synth WebAssembly-to-ARM compiler using SMT-based translation validation.

## Overview

This crate provides:

- **SMT-based translation validation**using Z3 SMT solver
- **Formal semantics**for WebAssembly and ARM operations
- **Property-based testing**framework with proptest
- **Automated verification**of synthesis rules

## Architecture

```
synth-verify/
├── wasm_semantics.rs      # WASM → SMT encoding (25+ operations)
├── arm_semantics.rs       # ARM → SMT encoding (processor state model)
├── translation_validator.rs # Equivalence prover (Alive2-inspired)
└── properties.rs          # Property-based tests (50+ properties)
```
## Usage

### Verifying a Synthesis Rule

```
use ;
use ;
// Create Z3 context
let ctx = create_z3_context;
let validator = new;
// Define a synthesis rule
let rule = SynthesisRule ;
// Verify the rule
match validator.verify_rule
```
### Batch Verification

```
// Verify multiple rules
let rules = vec!;
let results = validator.verify_rules;
for  in results
```
### Property-Based Testing

```
use CompilerProperties;
use *;
proptest!
```
## Verification Approach

### Translation Validation

For each synthesis rule `WASM_OP → ARM_OPS`, we prove:

```
∀inputs. ⟦WASM_OP⟧(inputs) = ⟦ARM_OPS⟧(inputs)
```
Using SMT solver:

- Create symbolic inputs
- Encode WASM semantics: `φ_wasm`
- Encode ARM semantics: `φ_arm`
- Assert: `φ_wasm ≠ φ_arm`
- Check satisfiability:
- **UNSAT**→ Proven correct
- **SAT**→ Counterexample found
- **UNKNOWN**→ Timeout

### Example: ADD Verification

```
; Symbolic inputs
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```
## Verified Operations

| Operation | Status | Method |
|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

## Dependencies

### Required

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

### System Requirements

Z3 requires either:

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

For development without Z3:

```
# Skip tests that require Z3
```
## Testing

```
# Run all tests (requires Z3)
# Run specific test suites
# Property-based testing with more cases
PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

## References

- **Alive2**: Automated LLVM verification (Lopes et al., PLDI 2021)
- **CompCert**: Verified C compiler (Leroy, POPL 2006)
- **VeriISLE**: Verified instruction selection (Nandi et al., PLDI 2020)
- **Z3**: Efficient SMT solver (de Moura & Bjørner, TACAS 2008)

## License

Dual-licensed under Apache-2.0 OR MIT

## Authors

PulseEngine Team

# thingd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thingd/0.47.0/thingd/

## Expand description

Core primitives for thingd.

This crate owns the durable engine boundary: object storage, append-only
events, and queue storage. The default implementation is in-memory, with a
feature-gated `SQLite` adapter available for durable object, event, and
queue storage.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sqlite` | No | Enables with FTS5 search, WAL mode, and auto-migration`SqliteThingStore` |
| `connectors` | No | Enables CSV/JSON file connectors for data import |

[§](https://docs.rs#example-in-memory)Example (in-memory)

```
use thingd::{MemoryEngine, ObjectStore, EventLog, MemoryObject, MemoryEvent};
let mut engine = MemoryEngine::new();
let obj = MemoryObject::new("users", "alice", r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
engine.put_object(obj).unwrap();
let user = engine.get_object("users", "alice").unwrap();
assert_eq!(user.unwrap().body, r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
let event = MemoryEvent::new("audit", "user.created", r#"{"user":"alice"}"#);
engine.append_event(event).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-sqlite--requires-sqlite-feature)Example (`SQLite` — requires `sqlite` feature)

```
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
{
    use thingd::{SqliteThingStore, ObjectStore, MemoryObject};
    let mut db = SqliteThingStore::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    db.put_object(MemoryObject::new("users", "alice", r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#)).unwrap();
    let user = db.get_object("users", "alice").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(user.unwrap().body, r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
}
```

Procedural macros for the euv UI framework, including the `html!` macro
